newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance appoints new president.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance appoints new president.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co., the troubled used-car loan company, said Monday that its board appointed a specialist in business reorganization as its new president, effective immediately.

Mercury, which last Friday said it was unable to pay $17 million in debt after reporting accounting irregularities, said it appointed William A. Brandt Jr., president and chief executive of Development Specialists Inc., as its new president, succeeding John Brincat, who resigned.
The company said Brincat resigned as Mercury's president and chief executive but would remain with the company as an employee and director, assisting Brandt with business operations.

"I appreciate the confidence expressed by the board," Brandt said in a statement. "My experience with turnarounds is that the first stage is critical and requires enormous focus, coordination and immediate information gathering to identify the most effective way to return a company like Mercury Finance to financial stability."

Mercury, whose stock lost about 86 percent of its value last week after it announced that it was forced to restate its 1996 earnings due to accounting irregularities, also said it was scheduled to meet its lenders in Chicago on Monday to discuss financing arrangements to meet the company's liquidity needs.
Last Wednesday, Lake Forest, Ill.-based Mercury said it found problems in its bookkeeping that caused it to overstate earnings by $90 million over four years.

On Friday, after trading in its stock had been halted for two days, the auto lender's stock tumbled $12.75 to close at $2.125 -- resulting in a loss of more than $2.2 billion in market capitalization.

It said Friday that as a result of downgrades from several debt-rating services, it would not be able to issue new short-term debt, known as commercial paper, to repay maturing debt and could not make the payments due Friday.
Standard & Poor's Corp. and Fitch Investors Service downgraded the company's commercial paper to a default rating.
A special committee of Mercury's board was formed to investigate the accounting problems.
